root_idea.summary: The root denotes following or coming after one thing or person.
root_idea.development: From the basic idea of following develop the rear rider or follower, successive occurrence, a subsequent consequence, rear-position terms, and related roles of assistance or succession.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Form I verb has a distinct Quranic occurrence and lexical use.
The Quranic active participle is presented under its supported singular citation form.
The Quranic active participle is a substantivized lexical form with its own Quranic occurrence.

senses.definition: To follow closely behind; to come after so as to draw near.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction رَدِفَ لَكُمْ, the following is interpreted as drawing near to the addressees or becoming close behind them.

senses.definition: Coming after in succession; arriving one after another.
senses.usage_conditions: This is one interpretation of مُرْدِفِينَ in the Quranic promise of angelic assistance.

senses.definition: Having others follow or accompany them; bringing successive followers as reinforcement.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression, the form is also explained causatively: one group or person is accompanied by others made to follow.

senses.definition: Going ahead of an army as a vanguard.
senses.usage_conditions: A further Quranic interpretation understands the مُرْدِفِينَ as those preceding the army and inspiring fear in the enemy.

senses.definition: The one that follows; in the Quran, the subsequent blast of the horn.
senses.usage_conditions: In 79:7 it is commonly understood as the second blast following the first. Another interpretation takes the referent to be the heaven and stars that follow in the ensuing upheaval.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ride behind someone on the same beast; to be another person's rear rider.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may also be construed with لِـ in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To overtake and pass someone, or to overtake and follow him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted explanation includes a textual uncertainty about whether the second action is passing or following.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For an event to follow another event; for a subsequent event to come upon people suddenly or overwhelm them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an affair or event that occurs after another, especially when the later event arrives unexpectedly or with overpowering effect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a beast to allow or be strong enough to carry a rear rider.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes the beast's capacity to bear someone riding behind another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mounting of locusts one behind or upon another, including the male on the female and a third on the pair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of locust mating and successive mounting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act as a king's rear associate, deputy, or substitute in the royal administration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The historical office included sitting or riding behind the king, representing him in his absence, and holding a defined share in war spoils.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Synonymy: the relation in which words or expressions signify the same thing in the same respect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a conventional term of lexicology and may apply to single words, compounds, or a word and an expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone ride behind or with oneself on the same beast; to place him behind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative construction concerns seating or carrying a rear rider.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make one thing follow another; to cause things to occur or proceed successively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe successive things or stars following one another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mutual following or succession; the condition of being consecutive in one's parts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people following one another and of any thing whose parts or instances occur successively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To engage in sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use of the reciprocal form; the construction is stated neutrally without restricting the participants beyond the source's usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid, help, or assist one another against someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal construction expresses mutual reinforcement or assistance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come behind someone; idiomatically, to seize or overpower an enemy by coming from behind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The latter use includes taking an enemy captive or killing him from the rear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask someone to let one ride behind him on his beast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form X construction expresses a request for a rear-riding place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sequent or follower of a thing; in the plural, followers, camel-drivers or relay drivers, and aids or auxiliaries.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The uses are connected with following in turn or taking another's place when he becomes fatigued; the term may also be applied particularly to stars that follow other stars.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two successive periods of night and day; by extension, the corresponding morning and evening periods.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The paired periods are called successive because each follows the other.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The consequence, sequel, or result of an event or affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression لَيْسَ لَهُ رِدْفٌ means that an affair has no consequence or subsequent result.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hinder part of a thing, especially its buttocks or posteriors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The anatomical use is not limited here to any one sex or class of object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The king's deputy or vicegerent, who could manage affairs, represent him, and occupy his place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The historical office also involved sitting or riding behind the king and receiving a fourth of the spoils on the army's return.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A designated star, including a bright star in Cygnus or a star near the Lyre; رِدْفُ الثُّرَيَّا may denote Orion or Gemini.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are astronomical names based on the relation of one star to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sailor stationed in the hinder part of a ship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The dual رِدْفَانِ is used for two such sailors.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lambs or kids born late in the season in which sheep or goats give birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term refers to young animals born toward the end of the relevant birthing period.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place on which a rear rider sits or rides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes the riding-place rather than the rider.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who rides behind another; also a follower or a thing carried behind a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In plural usage it can describe people who come one after another, as well as a bag or other object conveyed behind a rider.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A star rising in the east when its opposite star sets in the west, or a star facing a rising star.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This astronomical use defines the star by its successive or opposite relation to another star.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A late entrant in the game of maysir who brings an arrow after one or two players have won and asks that it be included among their arrows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can also refer to the person who enters after the slaughtered camel has been divided and is nevertheless allotted a share.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Palm-tree shoots; also overlying streaks or layers of fat in the hinder part of a camel's hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two applications are plural usages of رَادِفَةٌ and related forms.

cautions: The Form I occurrence is supplied by QAC at 27:72:5; the Lane text uses an older printed Quran citation that does not match that modern location exactly, so the QAC location is used here.

The interpretation of مُرْدِفِينَ in 8:9 is reported in several ways, including successive arrival, being accompanied by further angels, and preceding the army; these are retained as separate Quranic senses.
The interpretation of الرَّادِفَةُ in 79:7 varies between the subsequent blast and a cosmic referent involving heaven and stars.
